original_question: Let ∼g denote ordinary group-style conjugacy inside subgroups of a semigroup, and let ∼u denote unit conjugacy, where a ∼u b means that some unit u satisfies u^(-1)au = b and ubu^(-1) = a. Is ∼u the smallest semigroup conjugacy relation that is strictly larger than ∼g, in the sense that every conjugacy relation different from ∼g must already contain ∼u?
target_in_paper: Section 4, unnumbered question immediately before Theorem 4.1: after defining unit conjugacy ∼_u, the paper asks whether ∼_u is “the smallest conjugacy that does not equal ∼_G.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the two relations involved—group-style semigroup conjugacy ∼_G and unit conjugacy ∼_u—and it correctly targets the minimality question about ∼_u under inclusion, which is exactly the Section 4 question raised after ∼_u is introduced. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
missing_details: You should state what counts as a semigroup conjugacy relation: in the paper, it means an equivalence relation that agrees with ∼_G whenever the ambient semigroup is a group. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

You should state the order on conjugacies explicitly: for conjugacies ∼_1 and ∼_2, one writes ∼_1 ⊆ ∼_2 if, for every semigroup for which both are defined and all a,b, a∼_1b implies a∼_2b. Without this, “smallest” is not fully specified. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

The paper phrases the issue as whether ∼_u is the smallest conjugacy that does not equal ∼_G, not as whether it is the smallest one strictly larger than ∼_G; your parenthetical implication captures the intended order-theoretic meaning better than the phrase “strictly larger.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

The quantifier ranges over all semigroup conjugacy relations and arbitrary semigroups; the paper does not impose finiteness, inverse-semigroup, epigroup, or monoid hypotheses for this question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

To make the question fully stand-alone, define ∼_G exactly as the reflexive relation such that, for a≠b, one has a∼_G b iff a and b lie in a common subgroup H≤S and b=g^{-1}ag for some g∈H, and define ∼_u using the unit group U(S). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
refined_question: For an arbitrary semigroup S, let ∼_G be the reflexive relation such that, for a≠b, one has a∼_G b iff there exists a subgroup H≤S containing a and b and an element g∈H with g^{-1}ag=b. Let U(S) be the group of units of S, and define unit conjugacy by a∼_u b iff there exists u∈U(S) such that u^{-1}au=b and ubu^{-1}=a. Call a relation on semigroups a semigroup conjugacy relation if it is an equivalence relation and coincides with ∼_G whenever the semigroup is a group; order such conjugacies by inclusion, meaning ∼_1⊆∼_2 if a∼_1b implies a∼_2b for every semigroup and every a,b. Is ∼_u the least semigroup conjugacy relation distinct from ∼_G under this order? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
justification: The draft is close to the paper’s intent, but the nearest paper-faithful target is not one of the five numbered problems; it is the unnumbered Section 4 question introduced after the definition of unit conjugacy. Section 2 supplies the hidden machinery your draft leaves implicit—namely the precise definition of ∼_G, what counts as a semigroup conjugacy, and the inclusion order on conjugacies. With those added, the question becomes a sharp stand-alone restatement of the paper’s Section 4 sentence asking whether ∼_u is the smallest conjugacy different from ∼_G; the paper then answers this negatively through Theorem 4.1 and the surrounding examples. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
